<h2>SherlockEQ 0.6.5</h2>

<p>
  A correction-focused fix. In earlier versions, choosing an equalizer preset or
  editing bands by hand could quietly overwrite the hearing correction derived
  from your audiogram — leaving you listening through the preset alone. This
  release makes your audiogram correction its own layer that always stays
  applied: equalizer presets and manual tweaks now sit <em>on top of</em> it
  rather than replacing it. It also makes the on-screen curves easier to read.
</p>

<h3>Fixes</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>Your hearing correction is no longer overwritten by EQ presets or edits.</strong>
    The correction calculated from your audiogram is now kept separate from the
    equalizer, and the two are combined when you listen. Picking a preset,
    dragging bands, or clearing the equalizer changes only the equalizer — your
    hearing correction stays in place.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>An entered audiogram always produces a correction.</strong>
    Profiles that had an audiogram but were showing a flat correction — for
    example after clearing equalizer bands — now rebuild the correction from
    your stored thresholds automatically.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Improvements</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>A clearer picture of what you hear.</strong>
    The equalizer chart now shows a combined <em>Result</em> line — your hearing
    correction and equalizer together — as the main curve, with an optional
    <em>Breakdown</em> view that separates the correction and your equalizer into
    their own lines.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>Easier-to-read curves, per ear.</strong>
    Each curve type now has its own line style and each ear its own color, with a
    new on-chart legend that labels them. The encoding is designed to stay clear
    for color-vision differences.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>More complete in-app Help.</strong>
    New and corrected Help articles for Speech EQ, Advanced EQ, and Listening
    Comfort, with fixes to several documentation inconsistencies.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not diagnose,
  treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus, or disability.
  For concerns about your hearing, consult a doctor, audiologist, or licensed
  healthcare professional.
</p>
